entries.title: Resolution #2026-051: Supporting Responsible Governance of Youth Use of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots in Schools and Education
entries.summary: Adopted at the 2026 Annual Convention in Snoqualmie, Washington, carrying concerns raised by the ATNI Youth Committee. Urges Tribal and public schools to set strong ethical safeguards for artificial intelligence in education, supports policies that keep it a supplement to critical thinking, cultural education, language revitalization, Elders, and human relationships rather than a replacement, and urges state and federal governments to consult with Tribes on protections for American Indian and Alaska Native youth.

entries.title: Resolution #2026-039: The ATNI Energy Committee Supports the Formation of a Task Force on Artificial Intelligence (AI)
entries.summary: Adopted at the 2026 Annual Convention in Snoqualmie, Washington. Calls for a task force, operating under the ATNI Energy Committee or added to an existing ATNI task force such as data centers, to identify the common interests of member Tribes in artificial intelligence technologies, laws, and policies, propose a plan for outreach and education, and support Tribal consultation with federal, state, and local governments and AI companies.

entries.title: Resolution #2026-034: Endorsement of the Tiered Sovereign Data Framework (TSDF) as an ATNI-Recognized Standard for Indigenous Data Sovereignty
entries.summary: Adopted at the 2026 Annual Convention in Snoqualmie, Washington. Endorses the Tiered Sovereign Data Framework as an ATNI-recognized standard for Indigenous Data Sovereignty, authorizes its release as version 1.0 under a Creative Commons noncommercial share-alike license, and affirms its four tiers: T0 Open/Public, T1 Community Network, T2 Negotiated Partner, and T3 Sovereign Restricted. The endorsement obligates no Tribe to adopt the framework; each Tribe decides its own use.

entries.title: Resolution #2024-35: Calling for Tribal Leadership and Oversight in Electric Grid Governance and Electric Transmission Planning
entries.summary: Adopted at the 2024 Annual Convention in Ridgefield, Washington. Calls on states, regulators, utilities, and other decision makers to give Tribal electric utilities, Tribal energy development organizations, and Tribal elected leaders oversight and leadership roles in forming and governing a Western Regional Transmission Organization, calls for free, prior, and informed consent in transmission planning at every level, and asks the National Congress of American Indians to establish a national Tribal working group on these issues.

entries.title: Resolution #2024-23: Establishing an ATNI Task Force on Offshore Wind Projects
entries.summary: Adopted at the 2024 Midyear Convention in Canyonville, Oregon. Establishes a limited-duration task force to research offshore wind, propose policy to the ATNI membership, align advocacy, and support member Tribes in their own advocacy. Records concerns about impacts on Tribal culture, sovereignty, sacred sites, submerged cultural resources, water, fish, and migratory species, and authorizes the Executive Board to press for a halt, meaningful consultation, and funding for Tribal engagement.

entries.title: Tiered Sovereign Data Framework (TSDF)
entries.summary: The public repository of the Tiered Sovereign Data Framework, a standard that turns Indigenous Data Sovereignty principles into four data tiers with rules for sharing data, working with outside partners, and using artificial intelligence. It holds the standard, a tier decision guide, and supporting literature reviews under a Creative Commons noncommercial share-alike license. ATNI endorsed the framework in Resolution #2026-034.

entries.title: Wopasi Pazo Working Group
entries.publisher: Environmental Data Science Innovation and Inclusion Lab, University of Colorado Boulder
entries.summary: A working group of the Environmental Data Science Innovation and Inclusion Lab (ESIIL) at the University of Colorado Boulder, co-led with members from the Sicangu Lakota Treaty Council and Sinte Gleska University. The group is working to make environmental data more accessible to community members through intuitive interfaces and natural language. Its public site is at an early stage.

entries.title: Affiliated Tribes of Northwest Indians
entries.summary: ATNI’s official website, with membership, conventions, committees (including the Energy Committee), programs, adopted resolutions, and contact information. ATNI describes itself as dedicated to promoting Tribal self-determination and sovereignty.

entries.title: Harnessing Data Centers for Tribal Economic Development
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: DOE hub page for Tribal data center resources: fact sheet, site-pitch template, the July 2026 Tribal Data Center Exploration Cohort, and diligence questionnaires for Tribes and developers.

entries.title: Data Centers for Tribal Economic Development: Frequently Asked Questions
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Plain-language FAQ on land needs, HEARTH Act leasing, selling power by PPA, water use, and permanent versus construction jobs for Tribes considering data centers.

entries.title: Beyond Land Leases: Harnessing Data Centers for Tribal Economic Development (webinar)
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy
entries.summary: Webinar transcript including a Tribally owned data center operator (Forest County Potawatomi's Data Holdings) and discussion of long-term leases, HEARTH certification and on-site power.

entries.title: Tribal Sovereignty and the Data Center Boom
entries.summary: Survey of 2026 Tribal moratoria, bans and ownership models (Cherokee, Seminole, Eastern Band, Shoshone-Bannock, Hualapai, Potawatomi, Hoopa) with the legal issues Tribal governments should address.

entries.title: Data Centers in Indian Country
entries.publisher: Turtle Talk (Michigan State University Indigenous Law and Policy Center)
entries.summary: Running list of Tribal actions on data centers, with links to the Cherokee Nation task force report, the Seminole Nation resolution, Sault Tribe resolution and Tribally owned facilities.

entries.title: Report on the Impact of Data Centers on the Economy and Natural Environment of the Cherokee Nation Reservation
entries.publisher: Cherokee Nation, Principal Chief's Task Force on Data Centers
entries.summary: Tribal government task force report with a 1,593-response citizen survey (64% opposed to hyperscale data centers on the Reservation), plus land status, energy, water and air quality analysis.

entries.title: AI Data Center Deals on Tribal Lands Are Writing a New Playbook
entries.summary: Legal commentary on deal structures (lease, joint venture, integrated co-development), sovereign immunity waivers, HEARTH Act timelines, Winters water rights and value leakage.

entries.title: The Future of AI Runs Through Indian Country
entries.publisher: Payne Institute for Public Policy, Colorado School of Mines
entries.summary: Commentary arguing Native Nations should own and operate AI infrastructure, with recommendations on equity, sovereign permitting, workforce and safeguards against extractive terms.

entries.title: Colusa Indian Energy and Strata Expanse Announce Strategic Partnership to Develop AI and Energy Infrastructure Campus on Tribal Lands
entries.summary: Press release for a Section 17 Tribal energy corporation partnering with a data center REIT, tied to a long-running Tribal microgrid and a plan for more than 100 MW of on-site generation.

entries.title: Shoshone-Bannock Tribes oppose data centers on reservation, ceded lands and treaty areas
entries.summary: Reports a Fort Hall Business Council resolution opposing data centers over water, energy costs, treaty rights and cultural resources, extending to ceded lands and treaty-protected areas.

entries.title: How Native American Tribes Are Fighting Data Centers
entries.summary: Overview of Cheyenne and Arapaho, Cherokee, Kickapoo, Hualapai and Colusa decisions on data centers, including a paused project projected at 1,000+ jobs.

entries.title: As data centers eye Oklahoma, Tribes weigh the costs
entries.summary: Reports on Seminole, Muscogee, Cherokee and Osage deliberations, including the Google Project Spring minerals lease request and local water system stress.

entries.title: Data Center Watch: $64 billion of data center projects have been blocked or delayed amid local opposition
entries.summary: Original report cataloguing $18 billion blocked and $46 billion delayed US data center projects from May 2024 to March 2025, with common opposition themes.

entries.title: Data Center Watch Q1 2026 report
entries.summary: Finds at least 75 projects worth about $130 billion blocked or delayed in Q1 2026, opposition groups in 49 states, and statewide moratorium proposals in 14 states.

entries.title: Why community benefit agreements are necessary for data centers
entries.summary: Argues for enforceable, public community benefit agreements with specific terms on payments, jobs, water, electricity costs, exit fees and dashboards, with municipal examples.

entries.title: Community Benefits Agreement Template (data centers)
entries.summary: Model CBA with a community advisory board, public reporting dashboard, audit and non-retaliation provisions that Tribes could adapt to Tribal jurisdiction.

entries.title: Before Breaking Ground: A Local Government Guide to Better Data Center Policy and Community Benefits
entries.summary: Toolbox for governments negotiating with data center developers, with the first analysis of eight executed CBAs and a note on NDA secrecy.

entries.title: Decommissioning Data Centers: Avoiding Stranded Assets
entries.publisher: Columbia Law School, Sabin Center Climate Law Blog
entries.summary: Legal analysis of what happens when hyperscale data centers stop operating and how contracts and policy can allocate decommissioning and stranded asset risk.

entries.title: Large-load tariffs increasingly rely on upfront payments, exit fees, ramp schedules
entries.publisher: Utility Dive (reporting on LBNL and Brattle Group)
entries.summary: Summarizes an analysis of 55 large-load utility tariffs and the 18 mechanisms used to protect existing ratepayers from data center costs.

entries.title: What must happen for AI's trillion-dollar gamble to pay off
entries.summary: Examines whether hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending can be justified by earnings, with expert warnings about stranded data centers if revenue lags.

entries.title: Your Brain on ChatGPT (arXiv:2506.08872)
entries.summary: Preprint in which 54 participants wrote essays with an LLM, a search engine or no tools; LLM users showed the lowest EEG connectivity and essay ownership. The abstract reports no effect sizes and no peer review is stated.

entries.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Confidence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers
entries.publisher: CHI '25 (ACM); Carnegie Mellon University and Microsoft Research authors
entries.summary: Survey of 319 knowledge workers who shared 936 examples: higher trust in GenAI went with less critical thinking and higher self-confidence with more. The design is self-reported and associational, with no causal claim.

entries.title: Kestin et al. 2025: AI tutor versus in-class active learning, randomized crossover in introductory physics
entries.summary: Randomized crossover in one Harvard physics course with 194 eligible students: a designed GPT-4 tutor produced learning gains about double in-class active learning, with effect sizes of 0.63 to 1.3 SD. Results are limited to one course and a tutor built by the study team.

entries.title: Beware of Metacognitive Laziness: Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Learning Motivation, Processes, and Performance
entries.publisher: arXiv (Fan et al.; British Journal of Educational Technology listing)
entries.summary: Randomized study of 117 university students in four support conditions: ChatGPT improved essay scores but not motivation or knowledge transfer. The metacognitive-laziness risk is offered as a possibility to test, not a finding.

entries.title: How Teens Use and View AI
entries.summary: Survey of 1,458 US teens and parents (fieldwork 25 September to 9 October 2025): 54% of teens use chatbots for schoolwork help and 10% do all or most of their schoolwork with them.

entries.title: Nearly 3 in 4 Teens Have Used AI Companions (Talk, Trust, and Trade-Offs report release)
entries.summary: National survey of US teens aged 13 to 17: 72% have tried AI companions and over half use them at least a few times a month. The advocacy organization recommends that no one under 18 use them.

entries.title: OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026: Exploring Effective Uses of Generative AI in Education
entries.summary: OECD review reporting that generative AI benefits depend on pedagogy and that easier task performance can come at the cost of deeper learning. The page returned HTTP 403, so the date and findings come from search excerpts.

entries.title: Hawley Introduces Bipartisan Bill Protecting Children from AI Chatbots (GUARD Act)
entries.summary: Bipartisan federal bill to bar minors from AI companions, require all users to be told the bot is not human and lacks professional credentials, and create new crimes for knowingly giving minors companions that solicit or produce sexual content. The release gives no bill number and later action is unverified.

entries.title: New California 'Companion Chatbot' Law Imposes Disclosure, Safety Protocol and Annual Reporting Requirements
entries.publisher: Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom (law-firm summary)
entries.summary: California SB 243, signed 13 October 2025: known minors must receive AI disclosure and reminders at least every three hours, all users get suicide and self-harm protocols, a private right of action carries a $1,000-per-violation minimum, and annual reporting begins 1 July 2027.

entries.title: Washington State Enacts Law Regulating AI Companion Chatbots With Private Right of Action
entries.summary: Washington HB 2225, signed 24 March 2026 and effective 1 January 2027: hourly reminders for minors versus every three hours for adults, limits on sexual and manipulative engagement with minors, public self-harm protocols and a private right of action. The summary says it excludes narrowly targeted learning tools.

entries.title: Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth (Executive Order 14277)
entries.summary: Executive order creating a White House Task Force on AI Education and a Presidential AI Challenge, with a 90-day deadline for Education Department grant guidance and 120-day steps to prioritize AI in teacher-training grants.

entries.title: Final Priority and Definitions: Secretary's Supplemental Priority and Definitions on Advancing Artificial Intelligence in Education
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Education (Federal Register, 91 FR 18774)
entries.summary: Final grant priority on AI in education, effective 13 May 2026. The Department made no change in response to requests for federal safety and parental-consent rules, saying how best to communicate about technology-use safety is decided at state and local levels.

entries.title: FTC Section 6(b) Orders on AI Chatbots Acting as Companions (secondary summary)
entries.publisher: DLA Piper (law-firm summary; FTC release not retrieved)
entries.summary: The FTC issued fact-finding Section 6(b) orders to seven generative-AI companion providers by a 3–0 vote, covering product design, advertising, age limits, safety testing and complaints. It is not an enforcement action, though its findings may inform one.

entries.title: Response to Information Request: State Artificial Intelligence Guidelines (April 2026)
entries.summary: State and federal AI-in-education policy scan covering EO 14365 on state AI laws, Illinois S.B. 1920 and Nevada A.B. 406. Pages 1 to 3 give no count of states with K-12 AI guidance.

entries.title: AI in Tribal Education: Building Confidence, Capacity, and Sovereignty in the Age of Innovation
entries.publisher: American Indian Policy Institute, Arizona State University (TEDNA AI Webinar Series)
entries.summary: Slide deck for Tribal education leaders on verifying AI outputs, protecting sensitive Tribal and personal data, a six-step AI strategy and questions on data sovereignty. It is undated, with late-2025 file metadata.

entries.title: NCAI Response to Request for Information on the AI Action Plan (letter, 15 March 2025)
entries.summary: NCAI comment asserting that Tribal Nations hold inherent sovereign rights to set standards for AI data use, collection and ownership, based on resolution NC-24-008. It addresses federal AI policy rather than schools.

entries.title: Montana K-12 AI Guidelines (news summary, October 2025)
entries.summary: Summary of Montana's K-12 AI guidelines, which reportedly ask districts to honor Tribes' guidance on Tribal content and respect Tribal sovereignty over cultural materials and data. The 'first state' claim is unsourced, and the state document was not opened.

entries.title: Springer Nature Pulls Cited ChatGPT-in-Education Meta-Analysis
entries.summary: Coverage of the 22 April 2026 retraction of a 2025 ChatGPT-in-education meta-analysis over discrepancies in its pooled studies. Its effect sizes should not be cited, though the retraction does not by itself show that ChatGPT harms students.

entries.title: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of AI (August 2026 update)
entries.summary: Payroll-data study finding no broad AI job losses but employment for ages 22-25 in highly exposed occupations about 19% below its counterfactual. Descriptive, not causal.

entries.title: Evaluating the Impact of AI on the Labor Market: Current State of Affairs
entries.summary: Ongoing tracker finding no discernible economy-wide labor disruption since ChatGPT's release. Page content did not load in this pass, so verify the latest update.

entries.title: New data show no AI jobs apocalypse-for-now
entries.summary: Summarizes the Yale Budget Lab analysis showing a stable occupational mix 33 months after ChatGPT, while noting early-career workers may be affected first.

entries.title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Cadences
entries.summary: Usage and survey data on automation, worker expectations and job-loss concerns from about 9,700 respondents. Vendor-produced and not representative of the general population.

entries.title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Learning curves
entries.summary: Reports task coverage, US state-level convergence in per-capita AI usage and widening gaps between countries.

entries.title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Economic primitives
entries.summary: Includes a vendor model of AI-driven US labor productivity growth (about 1.0-1.8 points a year over a decade) and task success rates.

entries.title: Hyperscaler Capex 2026: $720B-$745B Guidance by Company
entries.summary: Secondary tracker of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta 2026 capex guidance drawn from earnings calls. Check primary filings before citing.

entries.title: Hyperscaler AI Capex 2026: $434B and the D&A Lag
entries.summary: Analysis of the gap between capex and depreciation, debt financing and concentration risk behind the bubble debate.

entries.title: AI's Absurd Spending Boom? Hyperscalers Are Spending 102% of Cloud Revenue on Capex
entries.summary: Reports UBS estimates of hyperscaler capex of $1.009 trillion in 2026 and capex near 102% of cloud revenue. Commentary piece with limited cash-flow detail.

entries.title: If AI is roiling the job market, the data isn't showing it, Yale Budget Lab report says
entries.summary: Covers the Yale Budget Lab position, Oxford Economics data that 4.5% of 2025 layoffs were attributed to AI, and 'AI washing' of layoffs.

entries.title: CUB: Sustained High PJM Capacity Prices Ramp Up Urgency for Data Center Reform
entries.summary: Gives PJM capacity prices from $28.92 to about $325 per MW-day across five delivery years and proposes cost-allocation reforms. Consumer-advocate source.

entries.title: PJM's capacity costs hit record as grid falls short on reliability
entries.summary: Reports a record $16.4 billion capacity cost for 2027-28, PJM's projection that data centers drive nearly all peak growth to 2030, and NRDC's bill projection.

entries.title: Are AI Datacenters Increasing Electric Bills for American Households?
entries.summary: Skeptical analysis arguing PJM market design and forecasting, not AI load alone, drive capacity price spikes. Partly paywalled.

entries.title: The Reality of Data Center Jobs
entries.summary: Opinion column summarizing Brookings, Virginia and Georgia findings that data center job promises are overstated, with a 20-30 jobs per 100 MW colocation benchmark.

entries.title: Have data center tax breaks helped Nevada's economy? Here's what we found
entries.summary: Examines $457 million of Nevada data center abatements against about 300 promised jobs and limited state tracking or audits.

entries.title: Potential Kentucky Data Center Sites by Region: State & Local Economic & Fiscal Impact Analysis (press release)
entries.summary: Industry-commissioned model of a hypothetical 400 MW campus projecting 200 permanent jobs and $290-435 million of local tax revenue over 12 years. Useful as the booster-side counterpoint.

entries.title: Resolution no. 45/2025: Support for a First Nations Approach to Artificial Intelligence
entries.summary: Carried at the December 2025 Special Chiefs Assembly, it calls for an OCAP-based First Nations AI data policy, a national AI and data strategy by December 2026, Free, Prior and Informed Consent before AI expands in government services, and funding for First Nations-led language AI.

entries.title: AI Data Centers and Tribes: Emerging Federal and State Policy Trends and Tribal Governance Options
entries.publisher: University of Oklahoma Native Nations Center for Tribal Policy Research
entries.summary: Sovereign Brief covering federal and state AI data-center bills, the Seminole Nation moratorium, Cherokee Nation's task force, and governance options for Tribes, with data current to May 2026.

entries.title: Seminole Nation moratorium on generative AI and hyperscale data centers
entries.summary: Reports the Seminole Nation Tribal Council's 24-0 vote of March 7, 2026 for a moratorium on generative AI and hyperscale data center development within Tribal lands; the duration is not stated.

entries.title: Cherokee Nation enacts AI policy to balance innovation with cultural protection
entries.summary: Describes Cherokee Nation's government-wide AI policy signed in August 2025, with permitted uses, quality review, fluent-speaker input on Cherokee-language work, and a governance committee that can approve, limit or ban tools.

entries.title: How Tribal governments are exploring AI use and regulation
entries.summary: Tribal officials describe a Morongo Band chatbot trained on past legislation, Cherokee Nation's AI policy and citizen survey, and the risk that a model could be trained on Tribal data.

entries.title: Co-Design Smart Disaster Management Systems with Indigenous Communities
entries.publisher: ACM Digital Government: Research and Practice
entries.summary: Participatory design study with the Omaha Tribe of Nebraska and Sac and Fox Nation of Missouri on an AI flood-damage reporting chatbot and drones, based on four emergency-manager interviews and two design workshops.

entries.title: Exploring Multimodal Foundation AI and Expert-in-the-Loop for Sustainable Management of Wild Salmon Fisheries in Indigenous Rivers
entries.summary: Preliminary video and sonar monitoring system developed with First Nations partners in British Columbia, reporting 81.2% mAP@50 for species identification against 72.5% for a YOLO baseline, with data-sharing agreements that give communities exit rights.

entries.title: Supporting Tribal-led salmon monitoring using computer vision
entries.publisher: University of Washington, Aeronautics and Astronautics
entries.summary: Describes a drone and AI project with the Sauk-Suiattle Indian Tribe to count Chinook redds across the Skagit watershed, with Tribal biologists and researchers hand-tagging drone images to train a redd detector; still in development at publication, with no timeline.

entries.title: Iwi leaders unveil AI safeguards to protect Māori data
entries.summary: Te Kāhui Raraunga's framework for AI and Māori data calls for bias monitoring, accountability, transparency and an exit option, and recommends an Algorithm Charter overhaul and an independent monitoring body.

entries.title: Māori algorithmic sovereignty: idea, principles, and use
entries.summary: Extends Te Mana Raraunga's Māori data sovereignty principles to algorithms and defines Māori algorithmic sovereignty principles for assessing existing algorithms or developing Indigenised ones.

entries.title: The CARE Principles
entries.summary: Explains the Global Indigenous Data Alliance's CARE Principles (Collective benefit, Authority to control, Responsibility, Ethics), which complement FAIR and were drafted at a November 2018 workshop.

entries.title: Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Position Paper
entries.publisher: Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Working Group (Honolulu)
entries.summary: Multi-author position paper that sets out Indigenous-centred commitments for AI design, including accountability to Indigenous communities first and recognition of many Indigenous perspectives.

entries.title: AI platform offers free grant-finding service to all Tribal Nations
entries.summary: Covers Syncurrent's AI grant-discovery partnership, which White Earth Nation has tested since early 2024, with free access for Tribes under a 10-year partnership. Grant writing is planned, and the vendor's claims are unverified.

entries.title: Onvkuce: Mvskoke audio and video database (MIT Solve listing)
entries.summary: Describes a planned searchable database of Mvskoke audio and video built on AI speech tools, from a 2025 Indigenous Communities Fellowship listing (search snippet; page not opened).

entries.title: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence (Executive Order 14365)
entries.summary: Executive order creating a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force and directing agencies to challenge or condition funding on state AI laws. Carves out child safety, data center infrastructure, and state use of AI from the preemption recommendation.

entries.title: America's AI Action Plan
entries.summary: Federal roadmap with more than 90 actions on AI innovation, infrastructure (data center and energy permitting) and international leadership.

entries.title: OMB M-25-22: Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government
entries.publisher: White House Office of Management and Budget
entries.summary: Federal guidance on how agencies buy AI, companion to M-25-21 on agency AI use; both replaced Biden-era memos.

entries.title: Senate Strikes AI Moratorium from Budget Reconciliation Bill in Overwhelming 99-1 Vote
entries.publisher: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
entries.summary: Official release on the 99-1 vote removing the 10-year ban on state AI regulation from the 2025 reconciliation bill.

entries.title: White House Releases National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
entries.summary: Legal analysis of the March 20, 2026 White House legislative recommendations urging Congress to preempt conflicting state AI laws.

entries.title: State AI laws under federal scrutiny: Key takeaways from the executive order establishing federal AI policy framework
entries.summary: Explains why an executive order alone likely cannot displace state AI laws and what the Task Force, Commerce review and funding conditions do.

entries.title: Colorado SB24-205 Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence
entries.summary: Official bill page for the Colorado AI Act, later delayed and then replaced by SB 26-189.

entries.title: Colorado Enacts Artificial Intelligence Replacement Law
entries.summary: Summary of SB 26-189, signed May 14, 2026, which replaces the Colorado AI Act with a disclosure-focused framework effective January 1, 2027.

entries.title: California SB 53, Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act, signed
entries.publisher: Office of the Governor of California
entries.summary: Governor's release on the frontier-model transparency law and the CalCompute public computing consortium.

entries.title: California SB 243 Companion chatbots (bill text)
entries.summary: Official text of the first state law on AI companion chatbot safeguards, including protections for minors.

entries.title: Texas HB 149, Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act: bill analysis
entries.summary: Official analysis of TRAIGA, effective January 1, 2026, with prohibited AI uses, a regulatory sandbox and an AI council.

entries.title: Montana SB 212, Right to Compute Act (enrolled)
entries.summary: Enacted text making government restrictions on private use of computational resources subject to a compelling-interest test.

entries.title: Washington State Artificial Intelligence Task Force releases final report
entries.publisher: Washington State Office of the Attorney General
entries.summary: Final report of the state AI task force with recommendations; four were enacted in whole or part, including companion chatbot regulation.

entries.title: Oregon SB 1546 (2026) Relating to artificial intelligence companions
entries.summary: Oregon AI companion chatbot law effective January 1, 2027, with disclosure, crisis-response and minor-protection duties.

entries.title: Avoiding the next digital divide: Defining digital sovereignty for Tribal Nations in the AI age
entries.publisher: Brookings Institution (with American Indian Policy Institute)
entries.summary: Defines Tribal Digital Sovereignty and describes Tribal AI policies and options for Tribal codes governing outside entities.

entries.title: Sovereign Snapshot: Tribal Nations and AI Governance, a selected overview of the AI risk regulation landscape
entries.publisher: Native Nations Center for Tribal Policy Research, University of Oklahoma
entries.summary: Reviews international, federal and state AI laws and notes that no federally recognized Tribe was believed to have adopted AI risk laws as of September 2025.

entries.title: Sovereign Brief: AI Data Centers and Tribes: Emerging Federal and State Policy Trends and Tribal Governance Options
entries.publisher: Native Nations Center for Tribal Policy Research, University of Oklahoma
entries.summary: Surveys federal and state data center policy and Tribal governance options, including the Seminole Nation of Oklahoma moratorium and Washington's data center working group.

entries.title: NCAI response to OSTP and NSF Request for Information on an AI Action Plan
entries.summary: NCAI recommendations that the federal AI Action Plan uphold Tribal sovereignty and Tribal data governance.

entries.title: Tribal Jurisdiction over Nonmembers: A Legal Overview
entries.summary: Explains the Montana v. United States exceptions that limit Tribal civil regulatory authority over non-members, relevant to regulating outside AI vendors.

entries.title: Through data governance, tribes protect digital land and build tribal economies
entries.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, Center for Indian Country Development
entries.summary: Reports on Tribal leaders discussing data governance, AI adoption and the legal infrastructure Tribes need for digital policy.

entries.title: ATNI 2027 Winter Convention
entries.summary: Dates January 17 to 21, 2027 at ilani Casino Hotel Resort in Ridgefield, Washington, with a registration link and draft agenda; the host Tribe is not stated on the page.

entries.title: ATNI 2027 Winter Convention draft at-a-glance agenda
entries.summary: Draft schedule, subject to change: five committee blocks, General Assembly sessions, State Caucuses, a Tribal Leader Policy Roundtable and a closing session on committee reports and resolutions. No energy summit or working-group block appears.

entries.title: ATNI 2026 Annual Convention draft agenda
entries.summary: Draft schedule for September 13 to 17, 2026 that includes an ATNI Energy Siting Project convening, an ATNI Energy Program and Siting Project update, an AI and Data Centers panel, and EPA Region 10 and incoming BPA Administrator agenda items.

entries.title: ATNI 2025 Energy Sovereignty Summit
entries.summary: Hosted by the ATNI Energy Program from September 3 to 5, 2025 at Snoqualmie Casino and Hotel, focused on funding options, workforce development and emerging opportunities. Partners and outcomes are not printed.

entries.title: ATNI Energy Committee 2024 Midyear agenda (email printout PDF)
entries.summary: Agenda for Energy Committee sessions at the 2024 Midyear Convention, covering BPA updates, DOE Office of Indian Energy and loan programs, Oregon and Washington state energy agencies, WSU, and a floated RTO resolution. The PDF contains personal contact details, which were not copied.

entries.title: Draft Priority Climate Action Plan, Affiliated Tribes of Northwest Indians
entries.publisher: Affiliated Tribes of Northwest Indians, prepared for U.S. EPA
entries.summary: April 2024 draft plan funded through EPA's Climate Pollution Reduction Grant planning program. It describes 57 member Tribes, resolution-based Executive Board governance, and power-sector measures on grid upgrades, transmission and wind feasibility.

entries.title: DOE announces contract selections for InterTribal organizations (Office of Indian Energy)
entries.summary: DOE selected ATNI and four other organizations for a $3.6 million pilot on DOE funding access and technical assistance for Tribes. ATNI would build an energy-project planning curriculum and provide a Tribal liaison; awards are pending contract negotiations.

entries.title: ODOE: 2023 NW Tribal Clean Energy Summit
entries.summary: Oregon Department of Energy staff presented and attended ATNI's 2023 NW Tribal Clean Energy Summit in Tulalip, Washington, which aimed to build Tribal capacity for energy project planning and energy sovereignty.

entries.title: Centennial Accord between the Federally Recognized Indian Tribes in Washington State and the State of Washington
entries.publisher: Washington State Governor's Office of Indian Affairs
entries.summary: Government-to-government accord signed August 4, 1989 that commits the state and Tribes to respect each other's sovereignty, meet annually, and escalate unresolved issues. The page does not state the accord's current status.

entries.title: Executive Order No. 13175: Consultation and Coordination With Indian Tribal Governments
entries.publisher: The White House (text hosted by the Federal Highway Administration)
entries.summary: Requires federal agencies to maintain accountable processes for meaningful and timely Tribal input on policies with Tribal implications. It favors consensual mechanisms, including negotiated rulemaking, on self-government, trust resources and treaty rights.

entries.title: CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance (copy page)
entries.summary: Presents the CARE Principles as people- and purpose-oriented principles that complement FAIR, drafted at a November 2018 workshop. The four element names are not on this page, and the 2019 date is inferred from linked file names.

entries.title: World Cafe to seek community input on Indigenous foodways
entries.summary: Preview of a July 21, 2026 community meal and World Café at Haskell Indian Nations University, developed by Indigenous leaders and knowledge-holders. The article reports no outcomes.

entries.title: M-25-36 Streamlining the Review of Deregulatory Actions
entries.publisher: Office of Management and Budget (Executive Office of the President)
entries.summary: OMB memo on streamlining deregulatory reviews; secondary summaries say it presumes EO 13175 consultation does not apply. The PDF could not be read in this pass, so the date and content need verification.

entries.title: Summary of Input from the 2013 Tribal Listening Forum
entries.summary: Summary of a 2013 California Tribal listening forum that cautions staff not to treat government-to-government consultation as public or stakeholder outreach. Seen in search results only, and the date comes from the file name.

entries.title: ATNI Resolution 2024-32: Rectifying the Dehumanization of Indigenous People in State Legal Systems
entries.publisher: Affiliated Tribes of Northwest Indians (copy in Washington courts Minority and Justice Commission materials)
entries.summary: ATNI resolution offered as a drafting example, identified from a search snippet that describes WHEREAS clauses. The PDF could not be parsed, so the clause structure and adoption details are unverified.

entries.title: Energy and AI: Energy demand from AI
entries.summary: IEA chapter estimating about 415 TWh of data-center electricity use in 2024 (about 1.5% of world electricity) and about 945 TWh by 2030 in its base case. It says China and the US account for nearly 80% of global growth to 2030.

entries.title: Key Questions on Energy and AI: Executive summary
entries.summary: IEA 2026 update: data-center demand grew about 17% in 2025 and is projected to roughly double by 2030 to about 950 TWh, with AI-focused demand tripling. It names gas turbines, transformers, chips and grid connections as constraints.

entries.title: 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report
entries.summary: LBNL report LBNL-2001637 estimating US data-center electricity use back to 2014, with a scenario range to 2028. The full text was not read in this review.

entries.title: Powering Intelligence 2026: Executive Summary
entries.summary: EPRI's February 2026 scenarios put data centers at 9-17% of US electricity by 2030. The page did not render in this review, so the figures come from search excerpts and need checking.

entries.title: Data Centers and Water: Frequently Asked Questions
entries.summary: CRS FAQ on data-center water use, including the lack of a systematic national water assessment. The PDF could not be parsed in this review, so its figures are unverified.

entries.title: Data center gas plants to boost U.S. power emissions by 20%
entries.summary: Bloomberg analysis of 99 planned gas plants in 22 states, estimated at about 318 million metric tons of CO2 a year. The article notes that some projects may never be built.

entries.title: Environmental Integrity Project data center power report (gas projects serving data centers)
entries.summary: Advocacy analysis of 74 gas projects that would supply data centers directly, estimated at about 143 GW and 662 million tons of greenhouse gases a year. It was not opened in full, so treat it as an advocacy estimate.

entries.title: Clean Air Act Resources for Data Centers
entries.summary: EPA resource page on data-center air permits: state and local agencies issue most permits, and the page covers the 50-hour emergency-engine allowance, the 500-hour default and 2026 permitting items.

entries.title: Portland General Electric's data center customers to pay more for electricity under landmark law
entries.summary: Explains Oregon's POWER Act rate class for data-center loads above 20 MW, with exit fees, renewable conditions and a low-income efficiency surcharge on the largest users.

entries.title: What the Data Center Boom Means for Washington Local Governments
entries.summary: Summarizes Washington's 2026 data-center bills: SB 6231 was enacted, HB 2515 did not pass, and the state workgroup's final report awaits Tribal consultation.

entries.title: New Jersey Enacts Energy and Water Reporting Requirements for Data Centers
entries.summary: Law-firm summary of P.L. 2026, ch. 75, which requires semiannual energy, cooling, backup-power and water reporting to the Board of Public Utilities for data centers of any size.

entries.title: California's 2026 Data Center Laws: What You Need to Know
entries.summary: Summarizes seven California data-center laws signed September 21, 2026, including water-use estimates (AB 2619) and energy reporting for facilities of 10 MW and more (AB 1577). None bans data centers or imposes a moratorium.

entries.title: Council releases initial 20-year forecast for Pacific Northwest electricity demand
entries.summary: The Council's 20-year forecast names data centers and chip fabs as the largest drivers, clustered mainly in Eastern Oregon, Eastern Washington and the Portland and Boise metros. It warns its numbers run high because they omit efficiency and demand response.

entries.title: Expert panel addresses data center energy efficiency, load flexibility, and water impacts in Pacific Northwest
entries.summary: Panel report on Pacific Northwest data-center cooling: one consultancy study found water-using cooling used about 6% less annual energy and 20% less peak demand than air cooling. Current codes largely ignore peak demand.

entries.title: Developers eye Native nations, Tribal communities for new data center projects
entries.summary: Reports Tribal Nation moratoria and bans, the LeChee Chapter's opposition to a proposed 1-GW facility near Page, Arizona over water, and a Tribal-owned microgrid firm leading data-center deals.

entries.title: Tribal Concerns Regarding U.S. Data Center Expansion
entries.summary: USET document from March 2026, known only from a search excerpt (not parsed), on Tribal concerns about data-center water, energy, sacred-site protection and government-to-government consultation.

entries.title: PJM board proposes backstop capacity auction, data center curtailment plans
entries.summary: PJM board's July 27, 2026 proposal for a 6.8 GW backstop auction capped at $555/MW-day, plus removal of new large loads without new supply from future demand forecasts.

entries.title: North Carolina approves diesel generator permits for Amazon data center
entries.summary: North Carolina air permits covering 649 backup and temporary diesel generators at an Amazon-linked site. The state said its air process cannot weigh where the facility is built or require cumulative modeling.

entries.title: Executive Order 14141: Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure
entries.summary: Biden-era order directing the Defense and Energy Secretaries to identify federal sites for AI data centers paired with new clean power. It is revoked by EO 14318 Sec. 4, so its Tribal-consultation clauses (Secs. 4(k)(i) and 7(e)) no longer apply.

entries.title: Executive Order 14318: Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure
entries.summary: Defines Qualifying Projects (at least $500 million capital, more than 100 MW of new load, national-security relevance, or designation), requires agencies to report categorical exclusions to CEQ within 10 days, and revokes EO 14141. The fetched text does not mention Tribal consultation, historic preservation or Indigenous lands.

entries.title: DOE Announces Site Selection for AI Data Center and Energy Infrastructure Development on Federal Lands
entries.summary: Names four DOE sites (Idaho National Laboratory, Oak Ridge Reservation, Paducah, Savannah River) for AI data centers and power, with solicitations to follow. It says DOE will engage partners in consultation with states, local governments and federally recognized Tribes.

entries.title: DOE request for applications for AI data centers and energy projects at Idaho National Laboratory (descriptive title)
entries.summary: Opens long-term leasing for AI data centers and power at Idaho National Laboratory, with initial applications due November 7, 2025 and rolling review after. The release does not mention Tribal consultation, cultural resources or NEPA.

entries.title: DOE request for proposals for AI data centers and energy projects at Oak Ridge Reservation (descriptive title)
entries.summary: Seeks proposals for two Oak Ridge Reservation sites for AI data centers with power, due December 1, 2025. The release does not mention Tribal consultation, cultural resources or NEPA review.

entries.title: NNSA selects Amentum for AI data center and energy project at Savannah River Site (descriptive title)
entries.summary: Selects Amentum to negotiate a phased lease for a 1 GW data center with about 2 GW of on-site generation; no lease is final. The release does not mention Tribal consultation or NEPA.

entries.title: DOE partnership for AI and power campus at the Paducah site, Kentucky (descriptive title)
entries.summary: Announces a privately funded AI and power campus, reported at over $100 billion, with 2 GW of new gas, up to 2.6 GW of batteries and 2031 completion, subject to Kentucky PSC approval. The release mentions no Tribal, cultural or NEPA review.

entries.title: FERC Orders Action on Co-Location Issues Related to Data Centers Running AI
entries.summary: FERC news item on the December 2025 action in the PJM co-location proceeding (EL25-49), which addresses large loads and co-located generation. FERC's page returned HTTP 403, so details rest on secondary summaries.

entries.title: Cost Transparency and Customer Protection Initiatives in FERC's June 2026 Show Cause Orders for Large Load Interconnections
entries.summary: FERC page on cost transparency and customer protection in the June 2026 show-cause orders to grid operators on large-load interconnection. The fetch returned HTTP 403, so the item is listed from search results only.

entries.title: FERC Show Cause Orders Seek to Accelerate Large Load Interconnections to the Grid
entries.summary: Law-firm summary of the June 18, 2026 show-cause orders, including the preliminary finding that tariffs may be unjust, unreasonable or unduly discriminatory, the August 17, 2026 response deadline and a pause option to November 16. It is secondary; the FERC orders were not opened.

entries.title: FERC Issues Notice Extending Comment Period for Proposed ANOPR on Interconnection of Large Loads to the Interstate Transmission System
entries.summary: FERC notice extending the comment period on the proposed rulemaking on large-load interconnection (docket RM26-4-000), which followed DOE's October 2025 Section 403 directive. The notice was listed from search results and not opened.

entries.title: Removal of National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Regulations
entries.summary: CEQ interim final rule removing its NEPA implementing regulations (40 CFR parts 1500-1508), leaving agencies to use their own procedures; a January 2026 final rule reportedly followed. The Federal Register page redirected and was not opened.

entries.title: ACHP Votes to Move Forward with Notice of Proposed Rulemaking
entries.summary: ACHP announces that members voted to advance a proposed rule revising the NHPA Section 106 regulations, which next goes to OIRA review. The page gives no change list, vote tally, or Tribal or THPO language.

entries.title: Summary of Executive Order 13175 - Consultation and Coordination with Indian Tribal Governments
entries.summary: EPA summary of EO 13175, the baseline federal order on consultation with Indian Tribal governments. Search results found no 2025-2026 rescission in agency materials.

entries.title: Selected Tribal Lands in 118th Congressional Districts
entries.summary: CRS report on Tribal lands by congressional district that, per a search summary, describes the federal trust duty as potentially reaching treaty rights, land and resources. The PDF did not extract, so that description is unverified.

entries.title: BPA Kickstarts Large Load Initiative Under 'Aggressive' Schedule
entries.summary: Paywalled preview of BPA's accelerated large-load work, including SPRINT for identifying substations with spare capacity and a final record of decision targeted for spring 2027. The preview mentions no Tribal consultation or comment periods.

entries.title: EPA Launches Clean Air Act Resource for Data Centers
entries.summary: Law-firm alert on EPA's December 11, 2025 Clean Air Act data center hub, its September 2, 2025 construction-timing letter, and which EPA changes remain proposals. It is secondary to EPA's own documents.

entries.title: Draft Ninth Power Plan identifies cost-effective resource portfolio to meet Northwest's energy needs by 2032
entries.summary: Announces the Council's draft Ninth Power Plan, with a 20-year load forecast and a proposed 2027-2032 resource portfolio. The page itself gives no data center megawatt assumptions.

entries.title: Draft Ninth Power Plan, Technical Appendix F: Electricity Demand Forecast
entries.summary: Sets out low, medium and high data center load trajectories and their contribution to system peak, about 1,600 MW in 2027 and 4,009 MW in 2046 averaged across futures. Notes the data may exclude smaller embedded data centers.

entries.title: Pacific Northwest Power Supply Adequacy Assessment for 2029
entries.summary: Tests 2029 adequacy with base (about 2,400 aMW) and mid (nearly 4,000 aMW) tech-load cases. Reports loss-of-load probability of 2.2% in the reference case and 13.3% in the higher data center case.

entries.title: 2026 Pacific Northwest Loads and Resources Study (2026 White Book)
entries.summary: BPA's regional loads-and-resources forecast. The 2026 edition cut near-term retail load because of the new large single load category and reports a firm-water surplus of 337 aMW in OY 2027 turning into a 3,514 aMW deficit by OY 2036.

entries.title: POWER Act Biennial Report: 2026 Oregon PUC Report to the Oregon Legislature
entries.summary: Oregon's first POWER Act report: data centers are about 15% of investor-owned utility load, projected at 25% by 2030, and PGE's compliance rates raise data center rates about 29%. Also covers municipal moratoria and federal large-load interconnection orders.

entries.title: Oregon governor orders pause on environmental permits to build or expand data centers
entries.summary: Reports Governor Kotek's Oct. 9, 2026 letter asking DEQ to hold air and water permits for new or expanded data centers until July 1, 2027. The page was blocked, so the details come from search-result text.

entries.title: City of Hillsboro, OR news item on data center moratorium
entries.summary: City item on the 120-day pause covering primary-use data center and battery storage applications. Per a search summary, the pause runs through Nov. 24, 2026 unless extended.

entries.title: Oregon utility tries out a faster, cheaper way to power data centers
entries.summary: Describes PGE's Hillsboro plan to connect about 80 MW of new data center load the following year using GridCARE software and a 31 MW battery, toward a 400 MW Hillsboro target by 2029.

entries.title: As Google's water demands grow, The Dalles aims to pull more from Mount Hood forest
entries.summary: Reports Google's rising share of The Dalles water (12% in 2012, about a third in 2024), the city's roughly $260 million water plan and the H.R. 655 land transfer for its reservoir.

entries.title: The Dalles drops fight to keep Google water use private
entries.summary: Reports the December 2022 settlement after a 13-month records fight, in which the city committed to release Google water consumption in future years with no frequency stated.

entries.title: Yakama Nation Data Center Findings and Recommendations
entries.publisher: Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation
entries.summary: The Yakama Nation's findings to Washington's Data Center Workgroup. They warn of 3,400-6,000 MW of added peak load under conventional cooling and of suspended salmon spill during emergencies, and note that several Tribes are evaluating data centers on Tribal lands.

entries.title: SPECIAL REPORT: How data centers pose a unique threat to Pac NW Tribes
entries.summary: Covers Tribal concerns about data centers, including exclusion from Washington's initial Workgroup, CTUIR's call for co-management of ceded-land siting, and the Goldendale pumped-hydro dispute. Contains culturally sensitive material.

entries.title: Salmon, Tribal sovereignty, and energy collide as US abandons Resilient Columbia Basin Agreement
entries.summary: Reports the June 2025 U.S. withdrawal from the 2023 Columbia Basin agreement, the Tribes' argument that it undermines treaty rights, and hydropower producers' citation of data center demand.

entries.title: Grant PUD & Data Centers: FAQs
entries.summary: Reports about 280 aMW of data center load in 2025 (about 37% of county load), an undated queue of about 800 MW, and the rule that data centers pay for the generation and wires built for them.

entries.title: Washington Legislature Punts Comprehensive Data Center Legislation to Next Year
entries.summary: Summarizes 2026 Washington data center bills: HB 2515 passed the House 51-41 but died in the Senate, and SB 5982, which applies clean-energy deadlines to large customers, passed with a governor's signature expected.

entries.title: Massive data center with power plant planned for public land in Idaho
entries.summary: Describes Rhea Data's proposed 4-million-square-foot campus on about 3,750 acres of BLM land near Boise, with a gas plant and no disclosed megawatt load. The project is pending federal review and sits outside Idaho Power's forecast.

entries.title: NorthWestern large-load data center tariff in Montana
entries.summary: Covers the Montana PSC's September 2025 position that NorthWestern needs approval to serve large loads, and advocacy groups' October 2025 call for a data center rate class, which they say could reach about 2,250 MW by 2030.

entries.title: Laws of Minnesota 2025, 1st Special Session, Chapter 12 (H.F. No. 16)
entries.summary: Enacted Minnesota data center law with a 100 MW definition, water permit conditions above 100 million gallons a year, a very-large-customer class due December 15, 2026, annual fees of $2 million to $5 million, and a sales tax exemption window ending June 30, 2042. Checked against the enacted text.

entries.title: Data Center Workgroup subgroup findings recommended to the full workgroup (draft)
entries.summary: Draft tax, energy and environmental findings: 37 states offer data center incentives, regional load projections, large-load cost-allocation options, and early-engagement recommendations for Tribes on treaty-protected resources. Undated; the file name suggests September 2025.

entries.title: Statement to Governor's Data Center Advisory Committee (CTUIR)
entries.publisher: Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation (posted on the Oregon Department of Energy site)
entries.summary: The Tribe's statement says its committee participation is not formal Tribal consultation and asks the Governor's Office to facilitate it later. It raises water, salmon, treaty-right and contracting-transparency concerns.

entries.title: Cherokee Nation issues Data Center Task Force report, new policy actions
entries.summary: Reports the Cherokee Nation's ban on hyperscale data centers on Tribal-owned and trust land, its consultation expectations for other land inside the reservation, and a recommended advisory committee.

entries.title: New Oregon Law Impacts Data Center Development Statewide
entries.summary: Law-firm summary of Oregon HB 4084 (2026): bars new data centers from Enterprise Zone exemptions from June 5, 2026 until 90 days after the 2027 session, grandfathers approved projects, and leaves the Strategic Investment Program open. Not the enrolled text.

entries.title: New York State Legislature passes first-in-the-nation data center moratorium
entries.summary: Summarizes S10642/A11560, passed June 4, 2026 (Senate 44-16, Assembly 102-39): a one-year pause on state permits for data centers of 20 MW or more. The governor had not announced a position as of July 1, 2026.

entries.title: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting
entries.summary: Describes Virginia's new water-utility reporting of monthly sales by customer category starting January 1, 2027, with facility-level data protected as trade secrets.

entries.title: After Local Zoning: Next Steps for Alaska in Data Center Development
entries.summary: Reports that Alaska SB 250 passed the Senate on May 16, 2026 and died in a House committee. It would have required commission-approved utility agreements that put service costs on data center operators.

entries.title: How New Law Transforms Large Load Power Projects in Texas
entries.summary: Law-firm overview of Texas SB 6 (2025) large-load interconnection standards, including the 75 MW threshold and curtailment rules. Not opened; details came from search excerpts and need checking against the statute.

entries.title: Washington Extends Data Center Sales Tax Exemption
entries.summary: A 2015 summary of S.B. 6057: data centers built July 1, 2015 to July 1, 2025 with a 12-facility cap. It is not evidence of any later extension.

entries.title: Data Centers and Water: Tribal Considerations
entries.publisher: Columbia River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission (posted by Oregon Department of Energy)
entries.summary: CRITFC slide deck on treaty fisheries, instream flows, aquifers, discharges and a transparency checklist for data center siting in the Columbia Basin. Slides carry a March 20, 2025 date, while the file name is dated 2026-03-27.

entries.title: Cherokee Nation bans hyperscale data centers on Tribally owned, trust lands
entries.summary: Reports the Cherokee Nation's ban on hyperscale data centers on Tribally owned and trust land, and its consultation condition for other reservation land. It cites a citizen survey of nearly 1,600 people with 64% opposed.

entries.title: More Tribal nations in Oklahoma are opposing, weighing data centers on their lands
entries.summary: Oklahoma Tribal positions on data centers, including Kickapoo opposition, Seminole's ban, Caddo's weighing and the Muscogee Nation's July 25, 2026 task force vote (12-3).

entries.title: As Data Centers Sidestep Tribal Consultations, Tribal Nations Are Fighting Back
entries.summary: Documents consultation disputes over STAMP in Genesee County, New York and an Alcoa East data center in Massena, and the federal permitting gaps that can bypass NEPA and Clean Water Act consultation. Its article date is not in the fetched text.

entries.title: Data Center Near Yellowstone River Would Cause 'Irreparable Harm,' Native Activist Says
entries.summary: Covers the Big Sky data center near Broadview, Montana, with about 1,700 MW of gas-fired generation, air-quality concerns for Fort Peck, Crow and Northern Cheyenne lands, and a water-well comment period closing October 29, 2026.

entries.title: Iron County approves zoning changes allowing large-scale developments amid Tribal opposition
entries.summary: Reports Iron County, Utah's unanimous approval of a development overlay that ended a data center permit pause early, over the Paiute Indian Tribe of Utah's objection that the county did not consult it.

entries.title: Colusa Indian Energy and Strata Expanse announce strategic partnership (AI and Energy Infrastructure Campus on Tribal Lands)
entries.summary: Company release announcing an AI and energy campus on Colusa Indian Community land with more than 100 MW of onsite generation planned within 18 months. It discloses no deal terms, site size or data center load.

entries.title: In Indian Country, Data Centers Come With a Familiar Threat of Colonialism. These Organizers Are Fighting Back.
entries.summary: Feature on Native opposition to data centers, including the Mvskoke Tech Park fight, the Stop Data Colonialism coalition and Honor the Earth's count of 106 or more proposed projects near Native land (advocacy figures).

entries.title: Mvskoke Tech Park plan crashes
entries.summary: Covers Muscogee (Creek) National Council bill NCA 25-077 for a tech park and data center on Looped Square Ranch, which failed 4-11 on November 15, 2025 after committee approval and a postponement.

entries.title: Amazon Agrees To Settle $20.5M Class Action Lawsuit Over Data Center Pollution In Eastern Oregon
entries.summary: Reports Amazon's proposed $20.5 million settlement of nitrate groundwater claims in Morrow and Umatilla counties, Oregon, where reporting attributes most of the rise to farm and food-plant runoff. No Tribe is named.

entries.title: Report sees data center load growth doubling or tripling 2028
entries.summary: Secondary summary of the LBNL report: 176 TWh (4.4% of U.S. electricity) in 2023, and a 2028 range of 6.7 to 12 percent of U.S. electricity. Verify these figures against the primary report.

entries.title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
entries.summary: Introduces federated learning, in which training data stays on devices and a shared model is built from device updates. Reports 10-100x fewer communication rounds than synchronized SGD across five architectures and four datasets.

entries.title: Small Language Models are the Future of Agentic AI
entries.summary: Position paper arguing that small language models suit many agent calls on capability and cost grounds. The abstract gives no parameter, hardware or benchmark figures.

entries.title: Abundant intelligences: placing AI within Indigenous knowledge frameworks
entries.publisher: AI & Society (Springer), via Massey University repository
entries.summary: Proposes Abundant Intelligences, an Indigenous-led and Indigenous-majority research program for rethinking AI through Indigenous knowledge systems. The abstract does not address data sovereignty or compute.

entries.title: Native Hawaiians developing sovereign AI data
entries.summary: Profiles Keolu Fox's proposed data terrariums, miniature data centers built from e-waste and powered by solar and wind, and argues for Native Hawaiians storing their own AI data on Indigenous land. The article gives no capacity or energy figures.

entries.title: Te Mana Raraunga: Māori Data Sovereignty Network
entries.summary: Māori data sovereignty network whose charter was approved in 2016. It distinguishes data sovereignty by storage location from Indigenous data sovereignty by collection location, and holds that Māori data should be subject to Māori governance.

entries.title: IEEE 2890-2025: Recommended Practice for Provenance of Indigenous Peoples' Data
entries.summary: Active IEEE recommended practice, published 2025-11-14, that sets common parameters for the provenance of Indigenous Peoples' data. Its public scope text does not mention AI or ML.

entries.title: Open Analysis and Synthesis Infrastructure for Science (OASIS)
entries.publisher: CU Boulder / CIRES, Environmental Data Science Innovation and Impact Lab (ESIIL)
entries.summary: Describes a shared platform for ESIIL teams offering common computing and AI tools. It does not say where computing runs and states no data-sovereignty or Indigenous-governance terms.

entries.title: Day-Ahead Market Policy: Record of Decision
entries.summary: BPA's May 2025 decision to pursue SPP Markets+ with responses to public comments. Section 8 (Tribal Obligations) sets out BPA's trust-responsibility reasoning, its position that FPIC does not apply to the market decision, and its commitment to government-to-government consultation on request.

entries.title: Proposed Decision to Join SPP Markets+ (letter to interested persons)
entries.summary: BPA's March 2026 proposal to join Markets+ with an October 1, 2028 go-live, describing the Wave 1 (October 1, 2027) and Wave 2 participants. Comments were due April 3, 2026.

entries.title: Bonneville Reconsiders Markets+ Choice and Considers EDAM
entries.summary: Reports BPA's September 3, 2026 letter to ROWE reconsidering its Markets+ choice in favor of CAISO's EDAM, with governance benchmarks and a draft decision targeted for year-end 2026. The article does not mention Tribes.

entries.title: EDAM Is Live: PacifiCorp and CAISO Launch New Market May 1
entries.summary: CAISO's release on the May 1, 2026 EDAM launch with PacifiCorp, including FERC approval of the design and tariffs and the 2027 and 2028 joining schedule.

entries.title: SPP's Markets+ Tariff Receives FERC Approval
entries.summary: SPP's announcement that FERC approved the Markets+ tariff, stating that Markets+ is expected to go live in 2027 and naming the Phase 2 participants.

entries.title: How ROWE Could Reshape Western U.S. Electricity Markets
entries.summary: Explains ROWE's board, stakeholder committee and public-participation design, including a 21-seat stakeholder committee with no reserved Tribal sector and a proposed Tribal Nations liaison role that is not yet final.

entries.title: WIEB Annual Summary: August 2025 to July 2026
entries.summary: WIEB's annual summary covering its staffing for WRAP's Committee of State Representatives and the Markets+ State Committee. Its board roster lists states, provinces and a vacant federal seat.

entries.title: West-wide Transmission Study 10-Year Horizon Report (WestTEC)
entries.publisher: WestTEC study, hosted by Western Power Pool
entries.summary: West-wide 10-year transmission study, released February 2026, identifying about 12,600 miles of 230 kV-plus upgrades costing about $60 billion. The full report was not opened; figures come from secondary summaries.

entries.title: WestTEC Results for Pacific Northwest Transmission Expansion
entries.summary: Council summary of WestTEC results for the Pacific Northwest, including 73 planned projects valued at $46.6 billion and a 20-year WECC plan targeted for fall 2026. Tribes appear only in a stakeholder list.

entries.title: Tribal Engagement in Transmission Planning
entries.summary: Technical report (NLR/TP-6A20-97009, 31 pages) on how Tribes can assess the importance of transmission and engage in planning. The abstract notes that about 2.3% of U.S. transmission miles are on Tribal lands.

entries.title: Tribal Engagement on Long-term Transmission Planning
entries.summary: CAISO's April 9, 2026 Tribal meeting deck on developing its Tribal Engagement Policy and on long-term transmission planning. Its slides state that CAISO is not a governmental entity.

entries.title: DOE Cancels Tribal Transmission Corridor Aimed at Bringing Reservation Power to Market
entries.summary: Reports DOE's August 12 decision to end the designation process for the Tribal Energy Access Corridor and two other corridors. It also covers the Oceti Sakowin Power Authority's account of Pine Ridge transmission costs.

entries.title: WRAP Binding Phase Set for Winter 2027/28 After Utilities Affirm Commitment
entries.summary: Reports that 11 utilities reaffirmed participation in WRAP and that the program is set to enter its first binding phase in winter 2027/28. The rest of the article is paywalled.

entries.title: BOEM Finalizes Wind Energy Areas in Oregon
entries.summary: Federal release finalizing the Coos Bay (61,204 acres) and Brookings (133,808 acres) wind energy areas, with about 2.4 GW of potential. It names Tribes as a source of feedback but describes no consultation process.

entries.title: Federal government rescinds Oregon's offshore wind energy area
entries.summary: Report that BOEM's July 2025 action removed the two Oregon zones, about 195,000 acres. Oregon officials said the decision does not preclude future offshore wind. Seen in search results; not fetched.

entries.title: BOEM Rescinds Designated Wind Energy Areas on the Outer Continental Shelf
entries.summary: BOEM notice rescinding all designated wind energy areas on the OCS (over 3.5 million acres, including California and Oregon), citing Secretary's Order 3437 and the January 20, 2025 presidential memorandum. It does not name Coos Bay or Brookings.

entries.title: Temporary Withdrawal of All Areas on the Outer Continental Shelf From Offshore Wind Leasing and Review of the Federal Government's Leasing and Permitting Practices for Wind Projects
entries.publisher: Federal Register (Executive Office of the President)
entries.summary: Federal Register publication of the January 20, 2025 presidential memorandum that withdraws all OCS areas from wind leasing and orders a review of wind leasing and permitting. Seen in search results; not fetched.

entries.title: Judge strikes down Trump's order blocking wind farm...
entries.summary: Report on the December 8, 2025 ruling by Judge Patti Saris (D. Mass.) that the January 2025 wind order was arbitrary and capricious, in a suit brought by a coalition of states and D.C. The page does not state the form of relief.

entries.title: Trump Administration Concedes Defeat on Wind Farm Freeze
entries.summary: Reports that the Justice Department dropped its appeal of the wind freeze ruling on June 15, 2026. It also summarizes the five California offshore projects affected and the status of Morro Bay leases as of June 2026.

entries.title: Federal government pays company $120 million to drop offshore wind power plans off the Central Coast
entries.summary: Report on the Golden State Wind lease surrender at Morro Bay for a $120 million federal payment that is conditional on a matching investment in Gulf Coast oil, gas, or LNG projects. Whether any money has been paid is not stated.

entries.title: California Sends Notice of Intent to File Suit Challenging Trump Administration's Unlawful Offshore Wind Deal
entries.summary: State notice of intent to sue over the Golden State Wind buyout under the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, with a 60-day window for the federal parties to respond. It also describes the similar Invenergy Morro Bay buyout.

entries.title: Elected Officials Outraged After Developer Vacates Humboldt Offshore Wind Lease
entries.summary: Local report on RWE's surrender of a Humboldt-area lease under a $1.22 billion Interior settlement, which the article describes as still to be paid. It also reports that a federal grant for the Humboldt Bay terminal was canceled.

entries.title: Oregon Offshore Wind Energy Roadmap
entries.publisher: Oregon Department of Land Conservation and Development (Oregon Coastal Management Program)
entries.summary: State roadmap required by HB 4080 (2024) that sets non-rulemaking standards for future offshore wind decisions, including protection of Tribal cultural and archaeological resources. Its draft comment period ran February 17 to April 27, 2026.

entries.title: Public comment extended on future of offshore wind in Oregon, including none at all
entries.summary: Report that the roadmap comment deadline moved to April 27, 2026 to reach residents who had not attended meetings. The roadmap then goes to the Legislature, and energy proposals could come up in the 2027 session.

entries.title: Oregon's offshore wind lease sale canceled as bidders back out, governor raises concerns
entries.summary: Report that the October 15, 2024 Oregon auction was canceled after only one of five qualified bidders stayed interested. Governor Tina Kotek asked BOEM to halt Oregon leasing and said Oregon would withdraw from the BOEM intergovernmental renewable energy task force.

entries.title: Southern Oregon tribes sue feds over offshore wind energy plans

entries.title: Anthropic Long-Term Benefit Trust

entries.title: Unleashing Tribal Energy Development (DE-FOA-0003548)

entries.summary: DOE Office of Indian Energy funding notice for Tribal energy development, including community-scale energy construction projects that serve Tribal electric loads. entries.title: Energy and Mineral Development Program (EMDP)

entries.summary: BIA grant program page for federally recognized Tribes and Tribal Energy Development Organizations to assess energy and mineral resources on Indian land, funding resource assessments and feasibility, market and engineering studies for resources that include biomass, hydro and geothermal. entries.title: AI3 Action Institute - Artificial Intelligence for American Indians (HHS-2026-ACF-ANA-NAI-0035)
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Native Americans (via Grants.gov)
entries.summary: Funding notice for one applicant to establish an institute that will track the pace of AI change, identify responsible and practical uses in Native communities and support AI integration across Indian Country. The listing shows $3.5 million; eligibility for federally recognized Tribes, incorporated state-recognized and non-federally recognized Tribes, Tribal consortia and Native nonprofits including Urban Indian Organizations; and an 08/27/2026 deadline, now closed.

entries.title: TechAccess: AI-Ready America (NSF 26-508)
entries.summary: NSF initiative to speed AI readiness and adoption nationwide through coordination, partnerships, hands-on assistance and workforce upskilling for businesses, public-serving organizations and individuals. The listing shows about $224 million in total, awards of $3 million to $4 million, unrestricted eligibility and a 07/16/2026 deadline, now closed.

entries.title: The Genesis Mission: Transforming Science and Energy with AI (DE-FOA-0003612)
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science (via Grants.gov)
entries.summary: Joint funding notice from the DOE Office of Science and five other DOE offices, including the Office of Electricity, for interdisciplinary teams using novel AI models to speed energy, environmental and nuclear research. The listing shows about $293.8 million in total, awards of $500,000 to $16 million, unrestricted eligibility and a 12/17/2026 deadline.

entries.title: Data Center Transparency Act (H.R. 6984, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: House bill to require reports on how data centers affect air quality and water quality, and on their electricity use. It was referred to the Energy and Commerce Committee on 01/08/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.summary: House bill directing the Secretary of Energy to study how data centers affect communities of color and low-income communities. It was referred to the Energy and Commerce Committee on 03/05/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026 (H.R. 8488, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: House bill to require developers of AI-focused data centers to disclose certain information before the facilities are developed. It was referred to the Energy and Commerce Committee on 04/23/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: H.R. 9019 (119th Congress): To direct the Secretary of Energy to report to Congress on the use of electric energy and water by certain data centers
entries.summary: House bill directing the Secretary of Energy to report to Congress on the electricity and water use of certain data centers. It was referred to the Energy and Commerce Committee on 05/22/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: S. 4559 (119th Congress): A bill to amend the Federal Power Act to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to issue a final rule relating to the interconnection of large load facilities with the transmission system
entries.summary: Senate bill to require FERC to issue a final rule on connecting large load facilities to the transmission system. It was referred to the Energy and Natural Resources Committee on 05/18/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2027 (H.R. 9022, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: House bill making FY2027 appropriations for energy and water development, the annual spending bill that funds the Department of Energy. It was placed on the House Union Calendar on 05/22/2026, and a House rule providing for its consideration was reported on 06/23/2026.

entries.summary: House bill to require states to include the physical security, cybersecurity and resilience of local distribution systems in their state energy security plans. entries.title: Water Power Research and Development Reauthorization Act (H.R. 7129, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: House bill to reauthorize water power research, development, demonstration and commercial application under the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007. A House committee ordered it reported, as amended, by voice vote on 05/20/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: Marine Energy Technologies Acceleration Act (H.R. 5692, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: House bill to accelerate U.S. competitiveness in marine energy technologies. It was referred on 10/06/2025 to the Science, Space, and Technology Committee and three other committees; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: Tribal Tax and Investment Reform Act of 2025 (S. 2022, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: Senate bill to treat Indian Tribal Governments the same as state governments for certain federal tax purposes. It was referred to the Finance Committee on 06/11/2025; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: AI Cyber Grid Protection Resilient Development Act of 2026 (H.R. 7696, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: House bill to create a grant program for National Laboratories and institutions of higher education to build secure AI cyber-physical testbeds that simulate grid-scale cyberattacks. It was referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection on 02/26/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: CHATBOT Act (S. 4407, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: Senate bill to require family accounts for children using AI chatbots and verifiable parental consent for teens. The Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee ordered it reported with a substitute amendment on 08/05/2026.

entries.summary: House bill to improve AI literacy education from kindergarten through grade 12. A House committee ordered it reported, as amended, by a 34 to 1 vote on 06/25/2026; a Senate bill of the same name (S. 4414) was referred to the Commerce Committee on 04/28/2026.

entries.title: NSF AI Education Act of 2025 (H.R. 5351, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: House bill to support National Science Foundation education and professional development related to AI. A House committee ordered it reported with a substitute by a 33 to 0 vote on 06/25/2026.

entries.summary: House bill directing the National Science Foundation to fund AI literacy programs. It was referred on 05/06/2025 to the Science, Space, and Technology Committee and three other committees; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.title: CREATE AI Act of 2025 (H.R. 2385, 119th Congress)
entries.summary: House bill to establish the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource. A House committee ordered it reported with a substitute by a 29 to 0 vote on 06/25/2026; a Senate bill of the same name (S. 4441) was referred to the Commerce Committee on 04/29/2026.

entries.title: S. 4627 (119th Congress): A bill to increase access to artificial intelligence through programs of the Department of Agriculture
entries.summary: Senate bill to widen access to AI through Department of Agriculture programs. It was referred to the Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry Committee on 05/21/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.

entries.summary: House bill requiring federal agencies to use the NIST AI Risk Management Framework when they use AI. It was referred to the Science, Space, and Technology Committee on 05/14/2026; GovInfo showed no later action as of 10/29/2026.
